matchups.recap: Rob got absolutely obliterated by 28.1 points this week—that's not a loss, that's a public execution. Flamur's team showed up ready to play football while Rob apparently showed up ready to take a nap, and it fucking shows in that 120-to-91 scoreline. You had one job: field a competitive roster, and instead you served up a masterclass in fantasy incompetence. Better luck next week, but let's be real—you'll probably need it.

Rinor got absolutely cock-blocked by 4.1 points—might as well have been 40 with how badly his lineup shit the bed when it mattered. You were so close to stealing this week that you could taste it, and then your receivers decided to go full ghost mode like they were auditioning for a horror movie. Better luck next week, pal, because this one's gonna sting worse than a paper cut on your nutsack.

Adam got absolutely skull-fucked this week, limping across the finish line with 108.8 points like he was dragging a dead horse through the fantasy wasteland. Nori's 121.5 was nothing special, but it didn't have to be—Adam's roster was so pathetic it made watching paint dry look like a shootout. That 12.7-point gap is the difference between "I have a functioning team" and "I should've autodrafted a damn AI instead of whatever hot garbage Adam assembled." Better luck next week, buddy, though frankly he's gonna need it.

Rilind got absolutely dicked this week, losing by 5.9 points like he was playing a pickup game against his younger cousin. That's what happens when your "strategy" is basically hoping your players don't actively sabotage you—spoiler alert, they did. Ben walked away with this one, and Rilind's looking at his roster wondering which of these bums is getting the first cut. Maybe next week won't feel like watching paint dry, but let's be real: it probably will.

Veton got absolutely skull-fucked by 16.2 points this week, and honestly, that margin is generous—it feels like he should've been down 30. This is what happens when you field a lineup that looked like it was assembled by a blindfolded monkey throwing darts at a waiver wire. Jetmir and Peter rolled into town with their shit together and left Veton wondering why he even bothered showing up. Better luck next week, chief—you're gonna need it.

Faton got absolutely skull-fucked this week, losing by 38.3 points like he accidentally started his entire bench while taking a shit. 79.7 points is what you score when your "studs" are actually duds and your waiver wire pickups are more washed up than a beach ball at a sewage plant. Ilir didn't even need to break a sweat—he just watched Faton's gameplan implode in real-time and coasted to an embarrassing blowout. Time to hit the trade market before what's left of your season goes full dumpster fire.

matchups.preview: Arben's rolling in at 4-0 like he actually knows what he's doing, but let's be honest—he's been running into a buzzsaw of injuries at other teams' skill positions. Rob's sitting 0-4 like a man who thought "wait until Round 6" was a legitimate RB strategy, and this week he's about to get absolutely demolished by whatever the football gods decide to throw at Arben's roster. Rob's the only thing standing between undefeated and 5-0, which means Arben's about to cover the spread by halftime.

Muriqi's sitting pretty at 4-0, but we all know that's just the league's way of building suspense before the inevitable collapse—dude's about to get exposed harder than a backup QB in primetime. Kastrati's only one game back and hungry as hell, and frankly, facing a team that's been getting carried by schedule luck is exactly the kind of matchup where the wheels fall off. This is where Muriqi learns the difference between padding wins against bottom-feeders and actually competing against someone who knows what the fuck they're doing.

Rinor's sitting at 2-2 with a roster that screams "I panic-picked at 3am," while Ben's somehow matching that record despite having actual talent—which is genuinely more embarrassing for him. This week one of you finally gets to feel like you know what you're doing, and the other gets to remember why their draft class was an absolute disaster.

Adam's barely clinging to life at 1-3, but don't worry—Veton's here to remind everyone what actual rock bottom looks like at 0-4. This is less a matchup and more a dumpster fire convention, where Adam gets to feel smug about his single win while Veton proves that even a broken clock is right twice a day. One of you is about to get embarrassed this week, and honestly, it could go either way because neither of you knows how to manage a roster.

Rilind's stumbling in at 1-3 looking like a man who thought "volume" was a legitimate fantasy strategy, while Faton's limping along at 2-2 with all the consistency of a broken slot machine. This is what happens when two teams with zero fucking clue meet in the middle—expect mediocrity, expect injuries to your best player the night before Sunday, and expect whoever's checking their lineup last at 11:58 AM to somehow still lose by 3 points.

Jetmir and Peter rolling in as a desperate 2-2 duo against Ilir's 3-1 squad—guess somebody's been doing their homework while you two have been drafting like you were hungover. This is what the family dinner table looks like for the next year if Ilir wins, and honestly? He probably will, because at least one of you two is going home with some serious explaining to do about how you managed to lose to the other Asllani.
